task_1.title: Fix Babel i18n entry point registration
task_1.description: Version 2.10.3 corrects a typo in the package metadata used for optional Babel i18n support so installation and Babel extractor registration work as expected for Jinja2 templates.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing the library with its Babel-based i18n support succeeds and that the Jinja2 Babel extractor is exposed under the expected entry point without being blocked by a misspelled extractor reference.

expectation.grounded: The package metadata for the `i18n` extra must publish a valid `babel.extractors` entry named `jinja2` that resolves to `jinja2.ext:babel_extract[i18n]`. Upgrading to 2.10.3 should remove the invalid extractor reference that could prevent installation or Babel from resolving the Jinja2 extractor.
expectation.conceptual: Users who install the library for internationalization should be able to install it cleanly and use Babel’s Jinja2 extractor normally, without failures caused by broken package metadata.

constraints.grounded: The fix is limited to the public Babel extractor registration used by the optional `i18n` dependency path. Existing package extras, the extractor name `jinja2`, and the intended Jinja2/Babel integration behavior must remain unchanged apart from correcting the invalid target reference.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only restore the intended installation and integration behavior for i18n users, without changing how users opt into internationalization or how the extractor is identified.

behavior: Installing the library with optional Babel i18n support should no longer fail because of a misspelled Jinja2 Babel extractor entry point.
The published `jinja2` Babel extractor entry should resolve to the intended Jinja2 extractor callable for i18n usage.
Babel-based integration that relies on the package’s registered Jinja2 extractor should discover the extractor through the standard entry point name.
acceptance_criteria: When a user installs version 2.10.3 with the optional i18n/Babel support, the installation should complete without being blocked by an invalid Babel extractor entry.
When Babel inspects registered `babel.extractors` entry points after the upgrade, the `jinja2` entry should resolve to the intended Jinja2 extractor target.
When a user configures Babel to extract messages from Jinja2 templates, the integration should use the package-provided `jinja2` extractor without packaging-related resolution failures.
